handbookNote: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151 (05/26)), published by the Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- fetched directly from https://mva.maryland.gov/Documents/DL-151.pdf on 2026-08-22 (11.6MB PDF, 319 pages, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/md_cdl_research/md_cdl_manual_full.txt, 12,151 lines) -- price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics: the manual's own front matter (Intro, page 9) explicitly confirms an 80% passing score is required per knowledge test (also the federally standardized minimum under 49 CFR 383.135(a), same as all other CDL-track states in this project), and that a failed knowledge test may be retaken after a minimum seven-day wait; the official MVA 'Knowledge Tests' webpage (https://mva.maryland.gov/licenses-ids/prepare-drivers-license-test/knowledge-tests, checked 2026-08-22) discloses exact item counts ONLY for non-commercial tests (e.g. Class C/M/Moped: 25 questions, 20 minutes, 88% to pass) and explicitly does NOT disclose item counts, time limits, or number-correct-to-pass for any CDL knowledge test (general knowledge or endorsement) -- it states only that CDL tests are computer-administered in English or Spanish. NEITHER the CDL manual NOR the official knowledge-tests webpage states an exact question count for the CDL general knowledge test or any endorsement test. Several third-party test-prep sites (cristcdl.com, epermittest.com, nextdoordriving.com, dmv-written-test.com) converge on '50 questions, 40 correct (80%) to pass, one hour time limit' for Maryland's CDL general knowledge test, but this figure could not be confirmed on any official MVA/Maryland.gov source and is therefore NOT asserted as fact anywhere in this question bank -- per this project's no-default-values discipline, this is explicitly hedged rather than borrowed from another state or an unverified third party. What IS confirmed directly from the official manual: Maryland has three CDL classes -- Class A (combination vehicles, GCWR 26,001+ lbs with a towed unit over 10,000 lbs GVWR), Class B (single vehicle GVWR 26,001+ lbs, or such a vehicle towing a unit of 10,000 lbs GVWR or less), and Class C (vehicles under 26,001 lbs GVWR that are either designed for 16+ passengers including the driver or require hazmat placarding) -- notably Maryland does NOT have separate D/E non-CDL license classes in this manual's CDL classification scheme; six CDL endorsements -- T (Doubles/Triple Trailers), P (Passenger Vehicles), N (Tank Vehicles), H (Hazardous Materials), S (School Buses), and X (Tank & Hazardous Materials combined); age minimums of 18 for intrastate CMV operation, 21 for interstate operation, and 21 to haul hazardous materials; only P, S, and N endorsements may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP), each with a mandatory companion restriction (P/S requires a P restriction; N requires an X restriction, i.e. no cargo tank); vehicles excluded from CDL requirements in Maryland include certain farm vehicles operated within 150 miles of the farm, emergency/fire apparatus, certain military vehicles, and recreational vehicles; intrastate medical waivers are limited to amputation/loss of limb, power grasping/prehension issues, and limited-eligibility deaf/hard-of-hearing cases, and are NOT available to holders of Hazmat, Passenger, or School Bus endorsements; School Bus (S) endorsement holders must obtain a new Medical Examiner's Certificate annually or the S endorsement is automatically removed; Maryland applies two distinct BAC disqualification thresholds -- 0.04% or more while operating a CMV disqualifies for 1 year (3 years if the vehicle was required to be placarded for hazmat) on a first offense, while 0.08% or more while holding a CDL (regardless of vehicle type being driven) also disqualifies for 1 year on a first offense -- both carry a lifetime disqualification for a second offense, as does refusal to submit to BAC/drug testing under Maryland's implied-consent law; the CDL Skills Test (administered by appointment only) consists of three parts taken in strict sequence -- Pre-Trip Inspection (45 minutes, including an air brake check if equipped), Basic Control Skills Test (10 minutes per maneuver, scored on points with 9 points a failure, automatic failure for hitting a curb or exceeding the time limit), and Public Road Test (35-40 minutes on average, scored on points with 31 points a failure, automatic failure for an accident or running a red light/stop sign) -- a driver must pass each part to advance to the next, and a retest fee applies after any failed portion; Hazmat endorsement applicants must complete a TSA fingerprint-based background check (out-of-state Hazmat CDL holders moving to Maryland must redo this check even if previously completed elsewhere) and must renew their TSA background/TWIC credential before expiration or the endorsement is automatically removed; Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) from an FMCSA-registered provider has been required since February 7, 2022 for first-time Class A/B applicants, Class B-to-A upgrades, and first-time School Bus/Passenger/Hazmat endorsement additions. Content-depth rationale: Maryland's manual reorganizes the standard AAMVA CDL content into its own 14-section structure -- Intro (licensing, classes, endorsements, ELDT, medical certification, disqualifications) plus Section 1 What You Need to Get Your CDL, Section 2 Knowledge Test Background (by far the largest section at ~94 pages, covering vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and all general-knowledge safe-driving topics -- split here into two buckets for volume), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split here into two buckets), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection Test, Section 12 Basic Control Skills Test, Section 13 On-Road Driving (Sections 12 and 13 combined into one bucket here), and Section 14 Slang Dictionary (a glossary of CB-radio/trucking slang terms not itself tested material and not used as a question source). Some sections (Cargo, Tank Vehicles, Doubles/Triples) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Maryland manual text or the official MVA knowledge-tests webpage cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
